# Test vectors

One directory per library. Every language's test suite reads these files and
must pass every case; a library is done in a language when it passes all of
them, not when it passes its own tests.

## Format

Each file is a JSON object:

```json
{
  "library": "moqom-token",
  "description": "What this file exercises, in a sentence.",
  "source": "Where the expected values came from (generated by which implementation, or the RFC section).",
  "cases": [
    { "name": "unique-within-file", "...": "inputs and expected outputs" }
  ]
}
```

- Bytes are lowercase hex, in fields ending `_hex`. Text is UTF-8 strings.
- Keys are given as seeds or private-key bytes so that signing is reproducible
  wherever the algorithm is deterministic ([ML-DSA-65](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/204/final) in deterministic mode,
  Ed25519). Where a signature is randomised (ES256), the vector gives the
  signature to verify, not one to reproduce.
- A case that must fail has `"error"` naming the failure class instead of an
  expected output. The classes are listed in each library's README, and every
  language maps its errors onto them.
- Times are Unix seconds in a field named `now`.
- Published vectors ([RFC 9605](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9605), [RFC 9420](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420), the MLS working group) are copied as
  they are, into a file named after their source, with `source` giving the URL.

Vectors are generated by `generate` programs checked in beside the library
that produced them, and regenerating must be a no-op unless the format changes.
